A pregnant mother says a single bite from her beloved rescue dog changed her family’s life forever... just weeks before she was due to give birth.

Sara Wood, 28, was 34 weeks pregnant when her three-year-old Staffordshire bull terrier, Blue, suddenly lunged at her face.

She had been playing outside with him and crouched down to tell him not to eat something dangerous.

In less than a second, everything changed.

Sara said Blue bit her lip, severing a vein and causing blood to spray across her face and pregnant belly.

“There was no barking, no growling, no jumping, no mauling or even head shaking,” she recalled. “It was just one clean bite and half of my lip was gone.”

She described the moment as a reaction rather than a prolonged attack, saying Blue appeared frightened immediately afterward.

“He tucked his ears and his tail and bowed down as if he was saying sorry that he didn’t mean to hurt me.”

Even while injured, Sara’s first concern was keeping her toddler calm.

She knew that, despite loving Blue, the safety of her children had to come first.

Animal control officers arrived within 10 to 15 minutes and restrained the dog before emergency medical workers could take Sara to hospital.

Doctors administered pain relief and antibiotics. Surgeons were unable to close the wound because there was no remaining piece of lip to reattach.

Sara was advised to keep the injury clean, moisturised, and covered until she could see a plastic surgeon three days later.

The family made the heartbreaking decision to surrender Blue to animal control.

They have not been told what happened to him since, but desperately hope he was assessed and might be given another chance in a suitable home.

For Sara, the physical injury was only part of the pain.

She was preparing to welcome another baby while grieving the sudden loss of a beloved family dog.

Blue had been part of her pregnancy and had been gentle with her older children, including her newborn daughter and toddler.

Her toddler still walks around the house calling, “Hi Boo,” looking for him.

Sara said the family plans to display Blue’s photographs, collar, bowls, and toys as reminders of the dog they loved.

“We lost a member of our family over an unfortunate mistake,” she said.

The family does not blame Blue or his breed. They simply made the decision they believed was safest for their children.

Their story is a heartbreaking reminder that even familiar, beloved animals can react unpredictably—and that responsible decisions sometimes come with unimaginable grief.
